headline: Symmetry is when parts mirror each other—a signal of health, beauty, and order across nature and art
universal_truth: Balance creates beauty; what matches suggests wholeness and health
fun_facts: Humans prefer symmetrical faces—symmetry signals genetic health and developmental stability
Most animals are bilaterally symmetrical, but starfish and jellyfish show radial symmetry
Snowflakes have six-fold symmetry because of how water molecules bond when freezing
discussion_questions: Why is symmetry so universally beautiful?
When is asymmetry more interesting than symmetry?
What areas of your life feel balanced versus unbalanced?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your face is roughly symmetrical—left matches right. Butterflies are symmetrical. Buildings are symmetrical. We find symmetry beautiful and use it in art and architecture. But why? What makes matching halves so universally appealing?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Symmetry appears everywhere in nature and human design. We find it beautiful without being taught to. Why does the brain respond so positively to symmetry?
cliff.prompt: Why do we find symmetry beautiful?

options.text: Symmetry signals health and order—asymmetry often indicates disease, damage, or disorder, so we evolved to prefer symmetry
options.response: Yes. Symmetrical bodies suggest healthy development. Asymmetry can signal illness or genetic problems. Our preference for symmetry may be an evolved health detector.

options.text: Symmetry is simpler for the brain to process
options.response: Processing ease is part of it, but the evolutionary signal of health matters too...

q1.title: Health Signal
q1.script: Developmental problems often cause asymmetry. Parasites, diseases, and genetic issues can disrupt balanced growth. Symmetry says: 'I developed correctly.' That's why symmetrical faces are rated as more attractive—they signal health.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Health Signal"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Types of Symmetry
q2.script: Bilateral symmetry: left-right mirror (humans, butterflies). Radial symmetry: multiple lines from center (starfish, flowers). Rotational symmetry: looks same when rotated (snowflakes). Different symmetries serve different purposes.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Breaking Symmetry
q3.script: Perfect symmetry can be boring. Artists often introduce slight asymmetry for interest—a face turned, a building with one tower. Dynamic balance—asymmetry that still feels balanced—can be more engaging than perfect mirroring.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Balance creates beauty. Symmetry teaches that what matches suggests wholeness and health. But don't fear asymmetry—sometimes breaking the pattern creates something more interesting.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 175. Tomorrow, we'll explore making flat things look deep—perspective. Until then, notice symmetry and asymmetry around you—in faces, buildings, nature, and your own life balance.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Balance Check - Symmetry in Life
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate balance in different life areas
growTrack.activity: Draw a line down a page. On each side, list matching pairs in your life: work/rest, giving/receiving, social/solitude. Are they balanced? Where is healthy asymmetry, and where does imbalance create problems? Life needs dynamic balance.
